data.title: Expedition Polish Hillforts 3 – Gdansk and the hillfort of Owidz
data.excerpt: The last day of our expedition belonged to the port city of Gdansk and to the Slavic hillfort of Owidz. Owidz, built in the 10th century on a moraine hill at a bend of the Wierzyca, has had its defences reconstructed along the whole circuit and is now a lively tourist destination.

children.text: The last day of our expedition belonged to the port city of Gdansk and to the Slavic hillfort of Owidz.

We went to Gdansk primarily because we wanted to see the Polish Baltic coast and to eat in the old town of Gdansk, and along the way we planned to visit the local archaeological museum. Unfortunately we were not lucky enough to see it, because it was being refurbished at the time and was therefore closed. All the more, then, did the old town of Gdansk surprise us. The extraordinary atmosphere, the omnipresent history, beautiful buildings, ancient ships, amber and the nearness of the sea make Gdansk a wonderful city for a long weekend at the very least. We were quite sorry that the other items on our programme meant we had to leave it after such a short time.
For a while we moved on to the Baltic coast, to the local beach, and enjoyed the cold sea, the sand and the whole northern seaside atmosphere.

blocks.alt: Expedition Polish Hillforts 3 - Gdansk and Owidz

children.text: From the beach we had to move rather unwillingly back into the car if we wanted to reach the last, but all the more important, stop that same day – the hillfort of Owidz. This Slavic hillfort lies on the top of a moraine hill, at a bend of the river Wierzyca. It was built in the 10th century and functioned until the 12th century. The remains of the fortress were used by Swedish attackers during the 17th century as a military camp. A large number of artefacts from the Slavic period of the Early Middle Ages have been found at the hillfort. Besides many pottery sherds, coins and amulets, a dog’s head was found here, buried at the entrance to one of the houses. Karolina Czonstke, one of the co-directors of the archaeological work, explained that the head of this dog had been sacrificed and buried beneath the doorway. “This ritual was meant to ensure the safety and well-being of the inhabitants of the house and to win the favour of the household spirits,” said Czonstke. The researchers maintain that, thanks to its good position, the settlement was wealthy and important. The hillfort lay on the trade route leading to Gdansk, a port city on the coast of the Baltic Sea.

blocks.alt: Expedition Polish Hillforts 3 - Gdansk and Owidz

children.text: The hillfort at Owidz was partly reconstructed in 2012 and is now a lively tourist destination. We were truly fascinated by the fact that the hillfort has its fortification reconstructed along the whole circuit. It also has several reconstructed early medieval houses and pagan idols. Partly thanks to the way it has been reconstructed, interesting living-history events are regularly held at the hillfort. We really did enjoy it to the full and stayed there until “closing time”. A very tasty dinner below the hillfort followed, and after that it was a straight line home.
